key_insight: A mixed Petrov–Galerkin Cosserat rod FEM can be discretized into a two-node rigid-body chain with compliant coupling, preserving robustness and no-locking behavior while matching discrete rod dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical rod model for soft robotics, tendon-driven systems, and slender-structure dynamics with simpler pairwise interactions than dense reduced-order formulations.
method: Represent the rod as rigid nodes connected by elastic force/moment couplings
Compute dilatation, shear, torsion, and curvature from relative node kinematics
Use a mixed compliance form with midpoint integration for internal work and trapezoidal rules for external/inertial terms
evidence_signal: Three numerical examples—piecewise cross sections, tendon actuation at different discretizations, and longitudinal-torsional dynamics—show accuracy, robustness, and convergence.
watch_item: The method depends on careful choice of quadrature and mixed variables; inconsistent implementation could compromise the intended no-locking behavior.
paper_title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
